original_question: For chromatic-polynomial zeros of graphs with maximum degree Delta, what is the optimal sharp bound C_opt(Delta) on their modulus, and what can be proved about zero-free or root-location regions in the complex q-plane beyond discs centered at q=0?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered open-problem discussion in Sokal’s chromatic-polynomial/complex-zero part of the q-coloring section: sharpen the linear-in-Δ disc bound for chromatic roots of bounded-degree graphs and identify stronger zero-free regions than a disc centered at 0. In later, more explicit formulations by the same author, this becomes the extremal-modulus question for graphs of maximum degree Δ (with K_{Δ,Δ} as the proposed extremal family) together with the conjectural zero-free region q > Δ(G), later strengthened to Re q > Δ(G).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right topic: chromatic-polynomial zeros for graphs with bounded maximum degree, the desire for the sharp modulus bound as a function of Δ, and the fact that Sokal’s discussion is not limited to crude discs centered at q=0 but also asks for stronger root-location or zero-free information.
missing_details: The graph class should be stated explicitly as finite loopless graphs G.
The polynomial should be named explicitly as the chromatic polynomial P_G(q) (or χ_G(q)).
Δ should be identified as the maximum degree Δ(G), and the quantifier should be 'for all graphs G with Δ(G) ≤ Δ'.
The sharp bound should be defined precisely, e.g. C_opt(Δ) := sup{|q| : P_G(q)=0 for some finite loopless graph G with Δ(G)≤Δ}.

The paper-faithful extremal candidate is missing: the later precise conjectural formulation is that, for Δ≥4, K_{Δ,Δ} should have the chromatic root of largest modulus among all graphs of maximum degree Δ.

The draft says 'beyond discs centered at q=0' too vaguely; the specific stronger region tied to Sokal’s discussion is the real zero-free interval q>Δ(G), later strengthened in Sokal’s later survey to the half-plane Re q>Δ(G).

If one mentions the optimal linear constant asymptotically, the natural lower-bound family and constant should be identified: K_{Δ,Δ} has a root αΔ+o(Δ), where α=-2/W(-2/e), so any universal linear constant is at least |α|≈1.598960.
The draft does not distinguish between a modulus bound, a zero-free region, and a full root-location description; the paper treats these as closely related but not identical questions.
refined_question: For each integer Δ≥2, let C_opt(Δ):=sup{|q| : P_G(q)=0 for some finite loopless graph G with maximum degree Δ(G)≤Δ}, where P_G(q) is the chromatic polynomial of G. What is the sharp value of C_opt(Δ)? In particular, is it true that for every Δ≥4 the complete bipartite graph K_{Δ,Δ} has the chromatic root of largest modulus among all finite loopless graphs of maximum degree Δ, so that C_opt(Δ) is attained by K_{Δ,Δ} (and hence has asymptotic slope |α|, with α=-2/W(-2/e))? Moreover, beyond such radial bounds, can one prove a universal noncircular zero-free region for all graphs with Δ(G)≤Δ—most notably the conjectured region Re q>Δ(G), or at least positivity on the real interval q>Δ(G)?
justification: The draft is aimed at Sokal’s chromatic-zero open problems, but it is broader and less precise than the paper’s actual intent. The 2000 survey states these issues informally in the chromatic-polynomial discussion rather than as a single numbered conjecture. The closest faithful sharpening is therefore to (i) define the extremal modulus problem exactly, (ii) name the specific conjectural extremal family K_{Δ,Δ}, and (iii) replace the vague phrase 'beyond discs centered at q=0' by the concrete stronger zero-free region that Sokal highlighted in this line of work, namely q>Δ(G) on the real axis, later strengthened by him to the half-plane Re q>Δ(G). I have not broadened the problem beyond bounded-degree chromatic roots, and I have avoided introducing unrelated Tutte-polynomial, matroidal, or dynamics variants except where needed to clarify the paper-faithful formulation.
